schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM Pension)
schemes.department: Ministry of Labour & Employment (enrolment through Common Service Centres, pension paid by LIC)
schemes.brief: A pension of Rs.3,000 a month from age 60 for workers who have no employer pension: labourers, street vendors, domestic workers, rickshaw pullers, farm hands, home-based workers and the like. You pay a small fixed amount every month from your bank account, from Rs.55 to Rs.200 depending on the age at which you join, and the Centre puts in the same amount again. You can join yourself on the Maandhan portal with a mobile OTP, or at any CSC with your Aadhaar and bank passbook.
schemes.benefit: Rs.3,000 a month pension from age 60; the Centre matches every payment you make
eligibility: Unorganised worker aged 18 to 40 years on the day of joining
Monthly income of Rs.15,000 or less
Not a member of EPF, ESIC or the government-funded NPS, and not an income tax payer
Must have a savings bank or Jan Dhan account with IFSC, and a mobile phone
Husband and wife can each join separately, and each gets a pension of their own
documents: Aadhaar card
Savings bank or Jan Dhan passbook showing the account number and IFSC
Mobile number (the OTP and payment messages come here)
Name and date of birth of your spouse and of your nominee
Cash for the first month's contribution if you join at a CSC (later months are auto-debited)

demoFields.label: Login as
demoFields.hint: Choose Self Enrollment. CSC VLE is only for the CSC operator, and Admin Login is for officials.

demoFields.label: Mobile
demoFields.hint: A number you always carry. The login OTP and every debit message come to this phone.

demoFields.label: Scheme
demoFields.hint: Pick PM-SYM. The other choice on the same portal, NPS-Traders, is for shopkeepers and small traders.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own Aadhaar. After the Aadhaar OTP, your name, date of birth and gender fill in by themselves, so check them.

demoFields.label: Occupation
demoFields.hint: The work you actually do every day, for example construction labourer, street vendor, rickshaw puller or farm labourer.

demoFields.label: Monthly income
demoFields.hint: What you earn in a normal month. It must be Rs.15,000 or less.

demoFields.label: Bank IFSC and account number
demoFields.hint: Your own savings or Jan Dhan account. The monthly amount is auto-debited from here, so keep enough balance.

demoFields.label: Spouse name
demoFields.hint: Husband's or wife's name. If you die before 60, your spouse can carry on paying or take the money out.

demoFields.label: Nominee name and relation
demoFields.hint: The person who gets the savings if both you and your spouse die.

demoFields.label: Self-declaration
demoFields.hint: You confirm you are not in EPF, ESIC or NPS and do not pay income tax. A false declaration gets the account closed.

demoSteps: Open the Maandhan login page, choose Self Enrollment and log in with your mobile number and OTP. Or go to a CSC with your Aadhaar and passbook, and the operator enrols you with your fingerprint.
Choose PM-SYM, enter your Aadhaar number and verify it with the Aadhaar OTP.
Fill in your occupation, monthly income, bank account with IFSC, spouse and nominee, and tick the self-declaration.
The portal shows your monthly amount for your age: Rs.55 at 18, Rs.100 at 29, Rs.200 at 40. Pay the first month and approve the auto-debit from your bank account.
Your Shram Yogi card with its Shram Yogi Pension Account Number (SPAN) is created. Download and keep it; an SMS confirms the enrolment.
Every month the same amount is auto-debited and the Centre adds an equal amount. Keep money in the account; missed months have to be paid later with a penalty.
From age 60, Rs.3,000 comes into your bank account every month. If you die after that, your spouse gets Rs.1,500 a month for life.

schemes.title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
schemes.department: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
schemes.brief: A guaranteed pension of Rs.1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 a month from age 60, for anyone aged 18 to 40 who has a savings account and does not pay income tax. You choose the pension, and a fixed amount is auto-debited from your bank account until you turn 60; the younger you join, the less you pay. After you, your husband or wife gets the same pension, and after both of you the nominee gets the saved amount. The Cabinet extended the scheme up to 2030-31 in January 2026; you can join online on eAPY if your bank is listed there, through your bank's net banking, or at your bank or post office branch.
schemes.benefit: Guaranteed pension of Rs.1,000 to Rs.5,000 a month from age 60
eligibility: Indian citizen aged 18 to 40 years
Has a savings bank or post office savings account; only one APY account per person
Not an income tax payer now or in the past (rule from 1 October 2022); if found later, the account is closed and the money returned
Pays every month, quarter or half-year until age 60, so at least 20 years of payments
Monthly amount depends on joining age: Rs.42 to Rs.210 at age 18, Rs.291 to Rs.1,454 at age 40
documents: Savings bank account number and IFSC (passbook)
Aadhaar card
Mobile number registered with Aadhaar
Spouse's name, and the nominee's name, relation and date of birth
For eAPY: Aadhaar OTP, Virtual ID, or the Aadhaar offline e-KYC ZIP file with its share code

demoFields.label: Whether Income Tax Payer
demoFields.hint: Choose No. Anyone who has ever paid income tax cannot join APY.

demoFields.label: Select your Bank
demoFields.hint: The bank where your savings account is. If your bank is not in the list (for example SBI), join through its net banking or at the branch.

demoFields.label: NLCC/Branch Name
demoFields.hint: The branch where your account is, as printed on the passbook.

demoFields.label: Bank Account Type
demoFields.hint: APY works only with a savings account.

demoFields.label: Bank Account Number
demoFields.hint: Copy it from the passbook. The monthly amount is debited from this account until you turn 60.

demoFields.label: Bank IFS Code
demoFields.hint: The 11-character branch code printed on the passbook or cheque.

demoFields.label: Please Select option (KYC)
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar or Virtual ID sends an OTP. Offline KYC needs the ZIP file downloaded from the UIDAI site and its share code.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Registered Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: The number linked to your Aadhaar; the OTP comes here.

demoFields.label: Pension Amount
demoFields.hint: The pension you want at 60. A bigger pension means a bigger monthly payment; the exact amount for your age is shown before you submit.

demoFields.label: Periodicity of Contribution
demoFields.hint: Monthly, quarterly or half-yearly. Monthly is easiest to keep up with on a small income.

demoSteps: Open the eAPY page and choose New Registration. Answer No to income tax, and pick your bank, branch, account type, account number and IFSC.
Choose Aadhaar, Virtual ID or offline KYC, enter your Aadhaar-registered mobile number and verify with the OTP; your details are taken from Aadhaar.
Pick the pension amount and how often you will pay, tick the consent for auto-debit, and fill the captcha.
On the next pages add your spouse and nominee, then confirm with OTP or eSign. Save the acknowledgement number that comes by SMS or email.
Once the bank verifies your account, you get a PRAN (Permanent Retirement Account Number) and the first amount is debited, so keep enough balance.
Keep money in the account on the debit date every time. A late payment draws a small penalty.
From age 60 the chosen pension comes to your account every month. After you, your spouse gets the same pension; after both, the nominee gets Rs.1.7 lakh to Rs.8.5 lakh.
schemes.helpline: 1800-889-1030 (APY toll-free, Protean CRA); your bank branch for debit problems

schemes.title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY / Sukanya Account)
schemes.department: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; run through India Post and authorised banks
schemes.brief: A savings account in a girl's name that pays one of the highest safe interest rates in the country, 8.2% a year for October to December 2026, completely tax-free. A parent opens it before the girl turns 10, at a post office or authorised bank, with as little as Rs.250, and keeps depositing for 15 years; the account matures 21 years after opening. Half the money can be taken out after she turns 18 for her studies. Rs.1,000 a month for 15 years grows to about Rs.5.5 lakh at today's rate.
schemes.benefit: 8.2% tax-free interest; deposit Rs.250 to Rs.1.5 lakh a year
eligibility: Girl child below 10 years of age, resident in India
Opened by the girl's parent or legal guardian; accounts opened by grandparents must be moved to a parent's name
One account per girl, and at most two girls per family (a third only for twins or triplets)
Minimum Rs.250 and maximum Rs.1.5 lakh in a financial year, paid for 15 years from opening
A year without the minimum deposit can be made good by paying Rs.250 for that year plus Rs.50 penalty
documents: Account opening form with Sukanya Samriddhi Account ticked
Girl's birth certificate
Parent's Aadhaar card
Parent's PAN card, or Form 60 if you have no PAN
Passport-size photos of the parent (and of the girl where the office asks)
Address proof, if the address on Aadhaar is different
First deposit of at least Rs.250, in cash or by cheque
schemes.submitAt: Any post office with a savings bank counter, or a branch of an authorised bank such as SBI, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank or ICICI Bank. Take the filled form, the girl's birth certificate, your Aadhaar and PAN with originals for checking, two photos and the first deposit of at least Rs.250; the passbook is handed to you at the counter.

demoFields.label: Name of Post Office
demoFields.hint: The post office or bank branch where you are opening the account. It can be moved to any other place in India later.

demoFields.label: Type of account
demoFields.hint: The same form is used for every post office savings scheme, so tick SSA.

demoFields.label: Name of account holder (girl)
demoFields.hint: The girl's name exactly as written on her birth certificate.

demoFields.label: Date of birth of the girl
demoFields.hint: She must be under 10 on the day the account is opened.

demoFields.label: Name of guardian and relation
demoFields.hint: The parent who will run the account until the girl turns 18.

demoFields.label: Guardian's Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar of the parent filling the form; show the original at the counter.

demoFields.label: Guardian's PAN
demoFields.hint: If you do not have a PAN, write Form 60 and fill that form instead.

demoFields.label: Mobile number and address
demoFields.hint: Messages about deposits and interest come to this number.

demoFields.label: Amount of first deposit
demoFields.hint: At least Rs.250. Later deposits can be any amount in multiples of Rs.50, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year.

demoSteps: Take the account opening form at the post office counter, or download it from the India Post forms page, and tick Sukanya Samriddhi Account.
Fill in the girl's details from her birth certificate and your own as parent, and attach copies of the birth certificate, your Aadhaar and PAN, with photos.
Hand it in with the first deposit. The clerk checks the originals and gives you a passbook with the account number.
Deposit at least Rs.250 every financial year for 15 years, at the counter, through the India Post or IPPB app, or by standing instruction.
Interest, 8.2% for October to December 2026 and revised every quarter, is added every 31 March and is tax-free. Deposits also count under section 80C in the old tax regime.
When she turns 18 or passes Class 10, up to half of the balance can be withdrawn for higher studies with the admission letter or fee slip.
At 21 years from opening, or at her marriage after 18, fill the closure form and the full amount is paid into her bank account.
schemes.helpline: 1800-266-6868 (India Post customer care); your bank branch if the account is with a bank

schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G Rural House)
schemes.department: Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development
schemes.brief: Money to build a pucca house for a village family that has no house or lives in a kutcha one: Rs.1.20 lakh in the plains and Rs.1.30 lakh in hill states, the North-East and difficult areas, paid into the bank account in instalments as the house goes up. On top of that the family gets 90 days of paid labour (95 in hilly areas) on its own house under the rural job scheme, and Rs.12,000 for a toilet. Families are picked from the SECC 2011 list and the new Awaas+ 2024 survey and checked by the Gram Sabha; homeless and destitute families, manual scavengers, primitive tribal groups and freed bonded labourers come first. The scheme runs till March 2029 for 2 crore more houses.
schemes.benefit: Rs.1.20 lakh (Rs.1.30 lakh in hill and NE areas), plus 90–95 days' wages and Rs.12,000 for a toilet
eligibility: Village family with no house, or living in a kutcha house (kutcha walls and roof, up to 2 rooms)
Name on the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List, or found eligible in the Awaas+ 2024 survey and passed by the Gram Sabha
Ruled out if any member owns a pucca house, a motorised 3- or 4-wheeler or mechanised farm machinery, or has a KCC limit of Rs.50,000 or more
Ruled out if any member is a government employee, earns over Rs.15,000 a month, pays income or professional tax, or runs a government-registered business
Ruled out if the family owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land with irrigation equipment, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land
Owning a two-wheeler, fridge, landline or motorised fishing boat no longer rules a family out (changed in 2024)
documents: Aadhaar card of the head of family and members (face e-KYC is done during the survey)
Bank or post office account seeded with Aadhaar
Job card under the rural employment scheme
Mobile number
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) number, if the family already has one
Paper for the plot where the house will be built (patta or possession proof); landless families are given land by the state
schemes.submitAt: Gram Panchayat office: tell the Panchayat Secretary or the Gram Rozgar Sahayak that you want to be surveyed under Awaas+ 2024, and take your Aadhaar, job card, bank passbook and mobile phone. The Block Development Office (BDO) registers the approved names; complaints go to the BDO or the District Rural Development Agency.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number of head of household
demoFields.hint: Checked by a face scan through the AadhaarFaceRD app; no fingerprint or OTP is needed.

demoFields.label: Name of head of household
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on Aadhaar. A woman head of family is welcome; the house is usually sanctioned in the woman's name or jointly.

demoFields.label: Family members
demoFields.hint: Add every member living and cooking together, each with Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Social category
demoFields.hint: SC, ST, minority or other. This decides which priority list your family goes into.

demoFields.label: Type of present house
demoFields.value: Kutcha walls and kutcha roof, 1 room
demoFields.hint: Describe the house as it is today. More than 2 rooms with a pucca roof makes the family ineligible.

demoFields.label: Monthly income of highest earner
demoFields.hint: The member who earns the most. Above Rs.15,000 a month rules the family out.

demoFields.label: Land owned
demoFields.hint: Write irrigated and unirrigated land separately, as in the land record.

demoFields.label: Photo of present house
demoFields.value: Geo-tagged photo taken in the app
demoFields.hint: Taken standing at the house, so the location is recorded with the photo.

demoFields.label: Job card number
demoFields.hint: From your rural employment job card. The 90 days of paid work on your house are booked against it.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: An account in the beneficiary's own name, seeded with Aadhaar. All instalments come here.

demoSteps: Ask at the Gram Panchayat whether your name is already on the Permanent Wait List, or look up the Panchayat-wise list on the PMAY-G website.
If it is not, get surveyed under Awaas+ 2024: the Panchayat surveyor fills the form on the AwaasPlus app, or you survey yourself on the app with a face scan where your state's survey is open.
The Gram Sabha reads out and checks the list, objections are heard at the block and district, and approved families are ranked by priority.
When your turn comes, the Block office registers you on AwaasSoft, geo-tags your old house and plot, and issues the sanction order. The first instalment comes into your Aadhaar-seeded account.
Build the house, at least 25 sq m with a kitchen. At each stage (plinth, lintel, roof) the official takes a geo-tagged photo and the next instalment is released.
Work on your own house under the rural job scheme for 90 (or 95) days' wages, and claim Rs.12,000 for the toilet through the Panchayat.
Finish within 12 months. Track payments with Search Beneficiary or FTO Tracking on the PMAY-G site, and go to the BDO if an instalment is stuck.
schemes.helpline: 1800-11-6446 (PMAY-G helpline) / support-pmayg@gov.in; Block Development Office for local complaints

schemes.title: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor Loan)
schemes.department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, with SIDBI
schemes.brief: A working-capital loan for street vendors with no collateral: Rs.15,000 first, then Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 once each loan is repaid. Repaying on time earns a 7% interest subsidy credited to your loan account, and taking and making payments by UPI or QR code earns cashback of up to Rs.1,600; vendors who repay the second loan can get a UPI-linked RuPay credit card. The scheme was restructured and extended in August 2025, and loans are given till 31 March 2030. You can apply yourself on the portal, or through a CSC or your municipal office.
schemes.benefit: Loans of Rs.15,000, Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 without collateral, with 7% interest subsidy
eligibility: Street vendor selling in a town or city, with a Certificate of Vending or ID card from the municipality or Town Vending Committee
Or named in the municipality's vendor survey (Survey Reference Number), even if no certificate was issued
Vendors left out of the survey, or from nearby villages and peri-urban areas who sell within town limits, can apply with a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from the municipality
Without an LoR, you must be a member of a vendors' association or have received the one-time Covid assistance
The Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 loans are given only after the previous loan is fully repaid
documents: Aadhaar card, with your mobile number linked to it (needed for e-KYC)
Certificate of Vending or vendor ID card, or Survey Reference Number, or Letter of Recommendation
Savings bank account passbook
Passport-size photo
Proof of membership of a vendors' association, if you have no LoR

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: Your Aadhaar-linked mobile. Fill the captcha and tap Request OTP; the OTP comes here.

demoFields.label: Vendor category
demoFields.value: In the survey, no certificate issued
demoFields.hint: Pick the line that fits you: have a certificate or ID card, in the survey without one, have an LoR, or none of these.

demoFields.label: Survey Reference Number (SRN)
demoFields.hint: Find it with the survey status search on the portal. With a certificate, give its number; with an LoR, upload it.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Verified by OTP; your name, date of birth and address are taken from Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Father's / husband's name
demoFields.hint: As on your Aadhaar or vending certificate.

demoFields.label: Social category
demoFields.hint: General, SC, ST, OBC or minority, as you belong.

demoFields.label: Vending details
demoFields.value: Fixed spot, Lajpat Nagar market, New Delhi
demoFields.hint: Where you sell and whether you sit at one place or move with a cart.

demoFields.label: Goods sold
demoFields.hint: What you mainly sell, for example tea, snacks, clothes, flowers or repairs.

demoFields.label: Lender and branch
demoFields.hint: Choose the bank where you have your savings account; the loan is credited there.

demoFields.label: Loan amount
demoFields.hint: The first loan is Rs.15,000. Rs.25,000 and then Rs.50,000 follow after repayment.

demoSteps: Check your name in the vendor survey on the portal and keep your SRN, certificate or LoR ready. Make sure your mobile number is linked to Aadhaar.
Open the PM SVANidhi login page, enter your mobile number and captcha, and log in with the OTP. A CSC or your municipal office can do this for you.
Choose your vendor category, complete Aadhaar e-KYC, fill in your vending and bank details, and submit. Note the application number.
The municipality verifies you; if you have no certificate, it issues the Letter of Recommendation online.
The bank approves the application and credits Rs.15,000 to your account. Repay it in monthly instalments over 12 months.
For on-time repayment, the 7% interest subsidy is credited to your loan account every quarter. Use UPI or QR for sales to earn the cashback.
After repaying, use Apply for 25k (18 months) and then Apply for 50k (36 months) on the portal; after the second loan you can apply for the RuPay credit card.

schemes.title: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY, First Job Rs.15,000)
schemes.department: Ministry of Labour & Employment, through EPFO
schemes.brief: A one-time payment of up to Rs.15,000 for people in their first PF-covered job: anyone who joins an EPFO-registered employer between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027, has never had PF deducted before, and earns up to Rs.1 lakh a month. There is no application form; the money comes from your employer's monthly PF filing, but only if your UAN was made with face authentication on the UMANG app and your bank account is seeded with Aadhaar. Half is paid after 6 months of work, and the rest after 12 months and a short online financial literacy course, kept in a savings deposit for a fixed period. It was announced in Budget 2024-25 as the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) scheme.
schemes.benefit: Up to Rs.15,000 (one month's PF wage) in two instalments
eligibility: First job with PF: you were never a contributing EPF member before 1 August 2025
Joined an EPFO-registered employer between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027
Gross salary up to Rs.1 lakh a month at the time of joining
UAN generated or verified with face authentication on the UMANG app
Stay with the same employer for 6 completed months (first instalment) and 12 months (second instalment)
Bank account seeded with Aadhaar; until it is, the money is held back
documents: Aadhaar card
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar
Smartphone with the UMANG and AadhaarFaceRD apps for the face scan
Bank account seeded with Aadhaar for DBT (ask your bank to link Aadhaar and enable DBT)
Your UAN, given to the employer when you join
schemes.portalName: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana portal (EPFO)

demoFields.label: UMANG service
demoFields.hint: Open the UMANG app, search for EPFO and choose UAN Allotment and Activation.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own Aadhaar. The UAN is tied to it for life, so you keep the same UAN in every job.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: The number linked to your Aadhaar; the OTP and later the UAN come here.

demoFields.label: Consent
demoFields.hint: You agree to share your Aadhaar details with EPFO.

demoFields.label: OTP
demoFields.hint: Type the OTP within the time shown on the screen.

demoFields.label: Face authentication
demoFields.hint: Install AadhaarFaceRD from the Play Store first. Look straight at the camera in good light and blink when asked.

demoFields.label: UAN
demoFields.hint: Comes by SMS. Give it to your employer's office so your PF and this payment are filed under it.

demoFields.label: Date of joining
demoFields.hint: Filled in by the employer. It must fall between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar-seeded bank account
demoFields.value: State Bank of India, account ending 9999
demoFields.hint: The money goes by Aadhaar to the account your Aadhaar is mapped to for DBT, which may not be the account in your PF record.

demoFields.label: Financial literacy course
demoFields.hint: Free and online. It must be done before the second instalment can be paid.

demoSteps: On your first job, make your UAN yourself in the UMANG app (EPFO > UAN Allotment and Activation) with Aadhaar, OTP and a face scan, and give the UAN to your employer.
Get your bank account seeded with Aadhaar for DBT at your branch. Without it the payment waits, though it keeps adding up.
Your employer files PF every month. Check in UMANG or on the EPFO member portal that your contributions are showing.
After 6 completed months with the same employer, the first instalment, half of one month's PF wage up to Rs.7,500, comes to your Aadhaar-seeded account.
Finish the free online financial literacy course on the EPFO portal before your 12th month.
After 12 completed months, the second instalment (the rest, total up to Rs.15,000) is put into a savings deposit in your name, to be paid out later.
If nothing arrives, call the EPFO help desk or file a grievance on EPFiGMS with your UAN.
